Stracka D.role: Co-author of two studies from Michael Hall's laboratory in Basel that placed mTORC2, the second mTOR complex, at the ribosome and at contact sites between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria
Stracka D.sub: Biozentrum, University of Basel (Hall laboratory, papers 2011–2015)
story: Daniele Stracka is second author on two Atlas studies from Michael Hall's group at the Biozentrum in Basel. The 2011 paper in Cell (ZIN2011) showed that mTORC2, the rapamycin-insensitive mTOR complex, is switched on when it binds the ribosome, the cell's protein factory, downstream of the growth signal PI3K. The 2013 paper in PNAS (BET2013) found that mTORC2 and its target Akt also sit at mitochondria-associated membranes, the contact points between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, where they help control how mitochondria work. Both studies are experiments in cells.

PubMed lists four papers under this name, all from the Biozentrum in Basel and all with the given name Daniele. The two Atlas studies themselves give no affiliation for him. The Basel link comes from the two other papers, so the evidence for the identity rests on the rare surname, the same given name and the same laboratory head in all four. No official page or current position was found.

highlights.ZIN2011: Second author of the paper showing that mTORC2 is activated by association with the ribosome.
highlights.BET2013: Second author of the paper placing mTORC2-Akt signalling at mitochondria-associated ER membranes.
